claims.statement: SFTP transfer responsibilities are separated so `SFTPTransferCoordinator` owns queued transfer runtime and admission, `SFTPTransferContext` owns a generation-scoped primary connection and lease topology, while `SFTPClient` is a connect/disconnect facade and `SFTPChannel` performs the file operations.

Transfer checkpoints are process-local: `SFTPResumeState` tracks a temporary path, source identity, acknowledged offset and SHA-256 state, and the coordinator pauses recoverable connection failures rather than silently replaying them.

Each transfer uses either a saved additional-connection snapshot, a managed transfer context, or an externally borrowed channel; saved connections are opened and disconnected per lease while a borrowed connection has no coordinator disconnect action.

Local uploads and remote copies preflight destination directories and targets before enqueueing; only after a conflict policy is selected do they resolve directory and target conflicts and enqueue resulting jobs.

Conflict policies can skip an item or subtree, replace a conflicting target, or select a next available Keep Both name and map descendants; replacement of a directory validates remote child names/paths and deletes children before their parent.

Same-host remote-copy planning rejects copying an item to itself or a directory into its own subtree, and copy execution streams directly between SFTP endpoints using shared-transport I/O or an in-process socket relay instead of local staging.

The process-wide scheduler grants logical-file permits under global and per-host limits, charges a cross-host copy once globally and once to each endpoint, rotates hosts then work sources while preserving FIFO within a source, and excludes overlapping exclusive borrowed resources.

SFTP preferences default to 30 global and 10 per-host transfers, normalize limits to supported ranges, and in Smart mode select channels for unknown sizes and files through 64,000,000 bytes but prefer connections above that threshold.

A transfer context keeps browser control channels independent where possible: channel-only work uses sibling channels or serializes the primary, connection-preferred work silently probes an additional connection and falls back to channels on non-cancellation failure, while cancelled probes do not cache the fallback capability.

Terminal upload resolution donates a successful independent preflight connection, falls back to the PTY SFTP channel only for a non-cancellation preflight failure, and does not fall back after cancellation or retirement.

Uploads and downloads use temporary destinations and source/prefix validation for explicit resume: uploads write a remote temporary then rename after checks, downloads commit a local temporary only after remote identity validation, and prefix SHA-256 mismatches fail resume.
Cancel or terminal failure attempts cleanup of the partial temporary file and surfaces cleanup failure with the partial path, whereas a paused transfer retains its checkpoint and partial destination.

Closing a pane releases only its transfer-context ownership: queued or active transfers retain the primary connection until references and slots drain; pausing a detached transfer permits closing that unused primary and explicit resume reacquires silently.

`SFTPEditService` tracks a managed temporary copy for a regular remote file, reuses it for a compatible repeated open, records route identity without credentials, and invalidates editing when the route or supplied connection destination changes.

External edit upload is explicit and conflict-checked: the service skips an unchanged digest, requires a replacement confirmation for a changed or insufficiently versioned remote target, binds confirmation to the observed version, and queues an immutable local snapshot only after validation.

Edit uploads pass an expected remote version and permissions into the transfer; the channel validates before temporary-file creation and again before rename, preserves permissions, and the service acknowledges only the snapshot digest so later local edits remain dirty.

Discarding an external edit stops tracking without deleting its local copy; active uploads cannot be discarded, paused uploads are cancelled and cleaned first, and host invalidation blocks further uploads while retaining local changes.

SFTP coordinator stores an admitted permit before reserving context slots and acquiring channel leases, and holds that file permit through I/O and lease cleanup; running can therefore include waiting for a channel.

The SFTP scheduler examines only each source queue's head while rotating hosts then sources, skips blocked heads without reordering within that source, and selects mode using current preferences at grant time without preempting active permits.

Coordinator copies anchor scheduling to the destination Host when available and use the destination managed context as workspace source, while ordinary managed transfers use their context and unmanaged transfers use batch identity.

Control, donated-preflight and PTY-fallback primaries have different leasing priorities; admitted overlap can choose extra connections or siblings, and context fallback waiters are resumed together rather than implementing source FIFO.

Managed browser-context extra connections and siblings disconnect on operation lease release rather than staying warm; saved and borrowed transfer forms bypass context topology selection, and a detached context can recreate an absent primary silently on explicit resume.

Agent SFTP data admission is conditional on schedulesDataTransfer, uses an agentRun identity, respects an externally supplied permit without double ownership, and obtains the authentication/channel lease within the admitted operation.

Agent SFTP reuses eligible idle pooled records, retains them on release and disconnects ephemeral siblings; its initial shared-probe catch records channel capability before rethrowing cancellation, unlike browser-context cancellation-before-downgrade behavior.

SFTP shared-transport copy compares driver identity rather than Host IDs and alternates reads of at most 64 KiB with writes; different driver identities use a concurrent socket-pair relay with coordinated cancellation.

Agent built-in SFTP read/write and scratch pull/push request logical-file admission, while SFTP metadata tools use the default non-data path; SFTP operations validate and normalize remote paths before using the authenticated pool lease.

Agent authentication acquires a scheduler permit before authenticating and leasing a channel for requested data work; it owns and releases only permits it acquired itself, and connection/authentication retries occur before, never after, the SFTP operation starts.

The Agent connection pool shares its Host-keyed primary SSH transport between exec and the primary SFTP subsystem across tool calls, joins concurrent primary opens, and invalidates reused connections on route changes or disappearance rather than reusing a connection to a different destination.

Agent route fingerprints describe destination, hops, identity, proxy, host-key trust and charset without reading Keychain secrets, so credential rotation alone does not retire an authenticated connection while removal of a temporary pane-backed target prevents further reuse.

Agent channel-only overlap leases siblings on the primary and, if sibling opening fails for a non-cancellation reason, waits for an idle primary; connection-preferred overlap probes silent extra connections and downgrades to sibling channels when silent setup fails, but propagates sibling failure on that path.

Agent pooled SFTP primary and auxiliary records become reusable on lease release while ephemeral siblings disconnect; idle sweeping removes idle auxiliaries and closes the primary with its exec connection only after no active leases remain and the idle timeout expires.

Disconnecting or invalidating an Agent Host cancels active SFTP lease tokens and disconnects channels and SSH transport; connection-loss errors after an operation evict the Host but do not replay the operation.

Agent authentication contexts are shared only among overlapping attempts for a Host and discarded with the last lease, allowing interactive authentication retries during connection setup without turning custom credentials into a persistent pool cache.

Agent sftp_copy obtains one destination-anchored permit charged to both endpoint Hosts and passes that permit into endpoint leases; same-host channel-only copies reuse one channel instead of opening a second endpoint lease.

MCP uploads are session-bound HTTP tickets with a separate upload budget and offset/length/token validation; their streaming SFTP transfer uses the Agent pool and file scheduler, not browser coordinator queue rows, while cleanup acquires a separate non-data SFTP lease.

MCP upload interruption or recoverable failure can pause an unexpired ticket for an explicit offset-matched HTTP retry, whereas integrity failure or cancellation triggers partial cleanup instead of silently replaying the upload.

Both app composition roots preserve saved SFTP concurrency preferences while applying a Pro-dependent MultiConnectionPolicy that makes the effective strategy channelsOnly without SFTP multi-connection access; later access changes update future scheduler admission without changing already-admitted permits.
